text:
claire: Quick sync — we need to lock down a measurement protocol for quantized runs that explicitly accounts for thermal vs power-capped behavior, KV cache state, and calibration overheads. I'm seeing noisy INT8/4-bit results across runs and want a reproducible playbook.

alex: +1. short checklist idea: (1) cold vs steady-state phases, (2) explicit power caps, (3) deterministic tokenization, (4) separate calibration dataset.

sumit: Can we be specific about the phases? I.e. how many warmup tokens / requests before we sample metrics? Thermal ramps can take multiple minutes on some racks.

claire: Proposal: two-phase runs per config. Phase A (cold): 10 single-request cold-starts with empty KV caches to measure startup overhead. Phase B (steady): one continuous run for 10 minutes using production-like request interarrival times to capture thermal/stable clocks + batching behaviour. Record p50/p95/p99 latency every 30s.

marie: Also add a prefill experiment: run the same steady workload but prefill KV with realistic prefixes (we should sample top-10 prefixes from prod trace). That exposes how prefix caching skews speed for large seq lengths.

jon: Important: calibration step (for INT8/FP8) often needs extra forward passes — that inflates wall-time if we include it in the runtime budget. Recommendation: separate the calibration phase and report: (a) calibration time & passes, (b) post-calibration steady-state perf. Calibration must not use any test prompts.

kevin: On power capping: run the steady-state experiment with at least three power limits: baseline (no cap), medium (manufacturer-recommended cap -10%), low (aggressive -20%). Use `nvidia-smi -i <GPU> --power-limit=<W>` and log clocks: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.gr,clocks.sm,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 1`.

claire: Good call. Also record GPU frequency governors and set persistence mode on to avoid frequency scaling noise: `nvidia-smi -pm 1`. Add the recorded clock traces to the run metadata for correlation.

alex: For kernel selection testing we need to sweep: batch sizes [1,2,4,8], seq lengths [128,512,1024,2048], and quant modes [fp16,fp8,int8,4bit]. But avoid combinatorial explosion — do stratified sampling and prioritize production-weighted cells.

marie: Tokenization: pin `tokenizers==0.15.3` and the model tokenizer commit hash. Small changes in tokenization can flip token counts and totally bias a fair comparison. Document tokenizer version in metadata.

sumit: Profiling tips: use CUPTI/Nsight for kernel-level breakdown during steady-state. Also capture `nvprof`-style summaries (or `nsys` export). Capture kernel durations, occupancy, and memory copies. When comparing quantized kernels, look for hidden memcpy spikes during KV cache spill/rebuilds.

jon: Metric list I want in every run: effective throughput (tokens/sec), tokens-per-joule (use power draw samples), p50/p95/p99 latency, KV hit/miss ratio, compilation/runtime kernel swap counts, and calibration error (if applicable).

kevin: For power draw sampling, run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=power.draw --format=csv -l 1` and aggregate mean/95. Use chassis-level PDUs if available for more accuracy.

claire: Reproducibility: seed workloads and record random seed and bench-bot run id. Bench runs should be repeated N=5 times and report mean and stddev. For each run store `dmesg` and `journalctl` snippets for the interval in case OOMs or drivers reset.

bench-bot: bench-run queued: id=Q-2312 model=llama2-13b-4bit batch=4 seq=1024 warmup=20 iters=500 power_cap=200W. Will post artifacts when done :white_check_mark:

marie: One more bias to watch: calibration and quantized kernels often change instruction mix and can cause different thermal equilibrium (so steady-state latency after calibration might differ). Suggest alternating order of configs across repeats to avoid systematic drift.

sumit: Agreed. Use Latin-square ordering when scheduling configs on the same machine. Also add a baseline fp16 run between quant configs to check drift over time.

jon: For fair accuracy/perf tradeoff reporting: always pair perf numbers with a small eval set (100 prompts) that measures key metrics (perplexity, exact-match on canned checks, and a few safety/formatting tests). Calibration must not see these eval prompts.

kevin: Commands and example run snippet for ops:
```
# set power cap
nvidia-smi -i 0 --power-limit=200
# enable persistence
nvidia-smi -pm 1
# run bench (example)
./run_bench --model llama2-13b --quant 4bit --batch 4 --seq 1024 --warmup 20 --iters 500 --log clocks.csv --tokenizer-hash abcdef123
```

claire: Output artifact list that must be archived per run: (1) raw perf CSV, (2) clock/power trace, (3) kernel profile (nsys), (4) tokenizer hash & model commit, (5) calibration artifact (weights/scale tables), (6) sampled prompts & responses for accuracy checks, (7) run metadata (seed, bench id, machine id).

marie: Can we add a small script to validate that KV prefill is deterministic and to measure prefill time? People often forget prefill cost.

kevin: I'll add a `prefill_check.py` to infra bench harness that runs prefixes and dumps the cache warmup time + hit rate.

claire: Decision items: 1) adopt two-phase run (cold + steady), 2) separate calibration and report calibration cost, 3) run 3 power caps and record clocks, 4) Latin-square ordering, 5) tokenize pinned. Any objections?

jon: No objections. Sounds robust.

sumit: SGTM. I'll draft a one-page runbook with commands and upload to the eng-runtime wiki.

kevin: I'll wire bench-bot to attach nsys exports to the artifact bucket automatically.

bench-bot: bench-run completed: id=Q-2312 artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/2024-06/Q-2312/ :rocket:

claire: Thanks all — let's iterate on the draft runbook and start ruthlessly prioritizing prod-weighted cells. If anyone sees a missing metric, shout here.

kevin: minor note — for FP8 kernels we should record the exact kernel variant string. We had two slightly different kernels last quarter and results differed by 5%.
